value.emollient_frequency: Non-medicated emollients or moisturizers allowed once daily in a stable regimen as normally used by the subject, applied only to untreated areas and only after study drug is applied to treatment areas
prohibited_concomitant: Approved biologics such as dupilumab (6-month washout)

Systemic treatments that could affect AD (corticosteroids, retinoids, calcineurin inhibitors, hydroxycarbamide, methotrexate, cyclosporine, azathioprine, hydroxychloroquine, mycophenolate mofetil, or other immunosuppressive therapies, or nonsedating antihistamines in a nonstable regimen) (4 weeks or 5 half-lives washout, whichever is longer)
Sedating antihistamines and OTC remedies containing sedating antihistamine (1-week washout)
Topical corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, or Eucrisa (crisaborole) (2-week washout)
Topical antibacterial medications/products including soaps, dilute bleach baths, sodium hypochlorite-based products anywhere on the body
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers (2-week washout)
Tanning beds/other light emitting devices (4-week washout)
All other investigational drugs (4 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer)
No rescue medication for AD is allowed during this study up to Week 4
Topical antibiotics, topical antihistamines, or any other topical agents may not be applied to treated areas
permitted_concomitant: Medications used chronically, in particular statins and anti-hypertensives, are allowed for use during the study except as specifically prohibited

Eye/ear drop and nasal corticosteroid preparations are allowed; inhaled corticosteroid preparations allowed if used for a stable condition and stable dose for >28 days before screening, continued at same dose throughout study
Non-sedating antihistamines (e.g. cetirizine, desloratadine, loratadine) in a stable regimen are allowed
Sunscreens allowed daily as needed, applied at least 2 hours after randomized study drug
Concomitant other medications for chronic conditions (e.g. NSAIDs, statins, anti-hypertensives) are permitted unless specifically prohibited
value.population_note: Monotherapy design (ARQ-151/roflumilast cream 0.15% vs vehicle QD for 4 weeks applied to all AD-affected areas) -- no standardized concurrent TCS regimen; the schema's TCS-flavored sub-fields (tcs_regimen/step_down_rule/recommended_agents) don't apply since topical corticosteroids are themselves prohibited concomitant therapy in this trial, not a background regimen.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 4.7.1. Prohibitions and Concomitant Therapy: Prohibited medications and products are detailed in Table 2 (Excluded Medications and Treatments)... Medications which have been used chronically by subjects, in particular statins and anti-hypertensives, are allowed for use during the study, except as prohibited in Table 2. No rescue medication for AD is allowed during this study up to Week 4. Table 2. Excluded Medications and Treatments [approved biologics/dupilumab 6 months; investigational biologics 6 months; systemic AD-affecting treatments 4 weeks or 5 half-lives; PUVA/NBUVB 4 weeks; topical urea 1 week; sedating antihistamines 1 week; TCS/TCI/Eucrisa 2 weeks; topical antibacterials; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers 2 weeks; systemic antibiotics 2 weeks; tanning beds 4 weeks; oral roflumilast 4 weeks; other investigational drugs 4 weeks or 5 half-lives].

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 6.5 Multiple Comparisons/Multiplicity: To control for familywise type I error at level of 0.05, the secondary endpoint of vIGA-AD Success at Week 4 for subjects with vIGA-AD score of 'Moderate' at randomization will only be tested if the primary endpoint demonstrates statistical significance... the remaining endpoints will be grouped into secondary endpoint family 1... and secondary endpoint family 2... An alpha level of 0.03 will be used to test the endpoints in the secondary endpoint family 1 sequentially. An alpha level of 0.02 will be used to test the endpoints in secondary endpoint family 2 sequentially... the Fallback Method will be applied... Should all 3 endpoints in Family 1 be statistically significant at the 0.03 level, then the full 0.03 alpha will be carried to Family 2. Family 2 would then be tested at the full (=0.02+0.03=0.05).

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Study Design: This is a Phase 3, parallel group, double blind, vehicle-controlled study in which ARQ-151 cream 0.15% or vehicle is applied QD for 4 weeks... Duration of Participation for Subjects: Screening (up to 30 days) + Treatment phase (4 weeks) for a total of about 8 weeks. Upon completion of the treatment phase of the study (Week 4/Day 29) subjects may have the opportunity... to participate in an open-label extension study (ARQ-151-313) of up to 12 months. Treatment Period and Clinic Visits: Week 1/Day 8, Week 2/Day 15, and Week 4/Day 29.
